diagnostics.message:
[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Splunk AWS integration is enabled with metric-stream synchronization but does not wait for the inline role policy granting CloudWatch metric-stream and iam:PassRole permissions to be attached. The delay after role creation does not establish ordering on this policy attachment.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Splunk AWS integration can be created before its metric-stream managed policy is attached. Its metric-stream integration requires these AWS permissions, and the provider documentation recommends ordering the integration after role-related policy resources; no attribute reference can express this ordering cleanly.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Splunk AWS integration enables CloudWatch metric-stream synchronization and relies on permissions granted by this inline policy, but it depends only on the IAM role and the delay. Ensure this policy is attached before creating the integration.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
signalfx_aws_integration.integration does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy (SplunkManagedMetricStreams), which grants the cloudwatch:*MetricStream* and iam:PassRole permissions the integration needs because it sets use_metric_streams_sync = true and enable_check_large_volume = true. Nothing in the graph orders that policy attachment before the integration is created (time_sleep only waits on the role), so Splunk Observability Cloud may attempt to validate/start metric streams against a role that doesn't yet have those permissions. Per the provider docs, role-related resources must be listed in signalfx_aws_integration's depends_on; add aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy there.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
signalfx_aws_integration.integration sets use_metric_streams_sync = true, which per the provider docs requires the IAM role to have the CloudWatch metric-stream actions and iam:PassRole — exactly the permissions granted by aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy. The integration does not depend on this policy, so it could be created before the metric-stream permissions are attached. It should depend on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
signalfx_aws_integration.integration sets use_metric_streams_sync = true, which per the signalfx provider docs requires the cloudwatch:GetMetricStream/PutMetricStream/DeleteMetricStream/etc. and iam:PassRole permissions that only exist in aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy. Yet there is no dependency (implicit or via the time_sleep gate, which only depends on the role itself) ensuring that policy is attached before the integration is enabled. The managed metric-streams integration can be activated against a role that lacks the required permissions.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
signalfx_aws_integration.integration sets use_metric_streams_sync = true, which the provider docs state requires the "cloudwatch:*MetricStream" and "iam:PassRole" permissions — those are granted only by aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy ("SplunkManagedMetricStreams"), which has no dependency path to the integration resource. If the integration is applied before this policy is attached, metric-streams mode can fail validation or leave the integration in a broken state. Add aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy to signalfx_aws_integration.integration's depends_on (or to time_sleep.wait_30_seconds, which it already waits on — this matches the provider docs' guidance to list role-related resources as dependencies of signalfx_aws_integration).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
signalfx_aws_integration.integration sets use_metric_streams_sync = true, which requires the cloudwatch:PutMetricStream / GetMetricStream / iam:PassRole permissions granted by aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy (SplunkManagedMetricStreams) — yet the integration has no dependency on that policy resource. With time_sleep.wait_30_seconds only waiting on the bare role, the policy attachment could race with (or land after) integration activation, causing the metric-streams setup to fail or the integration to come up non-functional. Per the provider documentation's guidance to depend on all role-related resources, add aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy to the resource's depends_on.

[merged-gpt-6-luna-atleast2of3]
[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run1]
The Splunk AWS integration can be created before the inline role policy granting its AWS inventory and data-collection permissions is attached. Add an ordering dependency so the remote integration is not provisioned before this policy.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run2]
The Splunk AWS integration can be created before its inline permissions policy is attached. Its metric-stream integration requires these AWS permissions, and the provider documentation recommends ordering the integration after role-related policy resources; no attribute reference can express this ordering cleanly.

----------------------------------------

[final-gpt-6-luna-effort-high-run3]
The Splunk AWS integration's role must have its inventory and service-read permissions attached before the integration is enabled. The existing dependency on the role does not guarantee that this inline policy has been created.

----------------------------------------

[merged-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-atleast2of3]
[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run2]
signalfx_aws_integration.integration is created without waiting for aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration (the SplunkObservabilityPolicy inline policy) to be attached to the role. The graph only gives it an implicit dep on aws_iam_role.splunk_integration (via role_arn) and an explicit dep on time_sleep.wait_30_seconds, and that sleep depends only on the role — so the policy can still be attaching after the integration is created. The Splunk Observability provider docs for signalfx_aws_external_integration explicitly say role-related resources created by Terraform must be added as dependencies of signalfx_aws_integration for correct ordering/cleanup, and that the role needs the permissions (e.g. cloudwatch:* for use_metric_streams_sync, iam:PassRole) when the integration is created and validated. Add aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration to signalfx_aws_integration.integration's depends_on.

----------------------------------------

[final-deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017-effort-high-run3]
signalfx_aws_integration.integration only depends on aws_iam_role.splunk_integration (via role_arn) and the time_sleep delay, but not on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration, which attaches the actual read permissions (EC2/CloudWatch/etc.) the integration needs to assume the role and pull data. If the integration is created before this policy is attached, its initial sync can fail. It should depend on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration.

----------------------------------------

[merged-glm-5.3-flash-atleast2of3]
[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run1]
signalfx_aws_integration.integration activates a cross-account CloudWatch/metric-streams integration that makes Splunk assume aws_iam_role.splunk_integration immediately, but it does not depend on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration. On creation the integration can be enabled before the SplunkObservabilityPolicy permissions are attached to the role, causing failed assume-role/API calls and a bad integration state. The signalfx provider docs explicitly require adding role-related resources (including policies) as dependencies of signalfx_aws_integration; the current gate (time_sleep.wait_30_seconds) only waits on the bare role.

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run2]
signalfx_aws_integration.integration enables the integration (enabled = true, import_cloud_watch = true) and depends on aws_iam_role.splunk_integration.arn, but nothing orders it after aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration is attached to that role. Splunk Observability validates the role's effective permissions when enabling the AWS integration, so the inline inventory/metric-read policy must exist first. Add aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration to signalfx_aws_integration.integration's depends_on (or to time_sleep.wait_30_seconds, which signalfx_aws_integration.integration already waits on — this matches the provider docs' guidance to list role-related resources as dependencies of signalfx_aws_integration).

----------------------------------------

[final-glm-5.3-flash-effort-high-run3]
signalfx_aws_integration.integration activates the Splunk AWS integration against aws_iam_role.splunk_integration, but has no dependency on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration (the SplunkObservabilityPolicy granting the account-inventory read permissions). Nothing orders the policy attachment before integration activation: time_sleep.wait_30_seconds only waits on the role itself, so Terraform may create the integration before the policy is attached, leaving Splunk's cross-account role session without the permissions it needs. The provider documentation explicitly requires adding role-related resources (including policies) as dependencies of signalfx_aws_integration; add aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration to the resource's depends_on.
